entries.intent: Define reusable parts from a relative anchor; instantiate them with explicit translation, discrete rotation or mirroring, and preserve occupied target structure with a non-air placement mask.
Establish large terrain form first, smooth and connect it second, and add bounded deterministic texture last; checkpoint before every bulk pass.
Use close evaluation for entrances and joins and distant compressed evaluation for silhouette, proportion, palette blocks and context; do not rely on showcase lighting alone.
Organize related materials as an ordered hue, value or temperature ramp with a deliberate direction instead of sampling an unordered random pool.
Validate the exterior shell before the interior pass; keep hidden lighting and other utility blocks on a separate layer that cannot leak into visible surfaces.
Reuse semantic components with their allowed orientation, connection and state fields, not only a block ID, and bind each component to its architectural role.
Assign frame, support, infill, surface and accent materials by per-face texture direction, continuity, border strength and visual weight rather than rarity or game name.
At small scale prioritize individual texture joins and available stair, slab and wall shapes; at large scale and distance prioritize the composition of major color fields.
Extract a source module only after its mass, opening and structural role work in the whole; record connection faces and repair gaps, overlaps, corners and support lines after transformation.
Keep repeated instances visibly related while varying selected width, height, opening, material or detail-density parameters; decoration must not conceal a weak repeated shell.
Give roof, frame, infill, base and accent explicit palette roles; use coordinated value contrast so structural lines remain readable without unrelated high-contrast noise.
Separate the building from ground and neighboring masses through value, hue, saturation or edge contrast; repeat a focal accent more quietly in subordinate locations so it reads as intentional.
Vary the proportions of role-bearing secondary masses, overlap them or share connection faces with the primary mass, and verify that the hierarchy remains readable from primary and corner views.
Partition oversized continuous walls with subordinate entrance, room, tower, dormer or shed volumes, concentrate detail at joins and focal areas, and preserve deliberate blank surfaces elsewhere.
Make tall masses, overhangs and links read as supported through a wider or stepped base, adjacent lower masses, or an explicit support path; do not invent a universal numeric ratio.

Assign every void a visible composition or spatial purpose and choose its base, middle, corner, top or full-layer position accordingly; reject cuts that flatten useful articulation or reduce readable hierarchy.
Preserve a continuous primary mass and clear solid-void hierarchy by merging or removing adjacent small cuts that have no independent role; do not invent a universal hole count or spacing.

Give base, middle and full-layer voids a visible support path appropriate to the material role; after translating, rotating or offsetting a cut volume, recheck joins, collisions, support and silhouette.
